data.narrative:
Zanskar, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Carl Hoiland and Joel Edwards, has raised $180M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M) alongside one public comparable and a broader universe of eight private frontier-tech peers in climate and energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses the $180M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $306M. The peer-median method anchors to the three same-stage, same-sector comparables, which show a median valuation of $1.0B with a range of $700M to $3.0B. This wider peer range reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity across the cohort.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $260M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $653M. The 4.3x spread between endpoints reflects material uncertainty in both stage-appropriate multiples and the appropriate peer comparables. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Zanskar's technology and market position warrant valuation at the median versus the tails of the peer distribution, and whether stage-progression or peer-benchmarking provides a more reliable signal in a capital-intensive, pre-revenue or early-revenue climate-tech landscape.
